clue.text: Carp about piano in work unduly devoted to fashion

indicators.note: the fish word goes round the rest, so 'about' marks it as the container here

parts.note: a carp is a kind of fish

indicators.note: the piano letter sits inside the work abbreviation, as 'in' says

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a musical work
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning soft

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles about a piano in a musical work that seems too concerned with style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carp' looks like a verb meaning complain, but here it is the fish, and 'about' and 'in' are both container signals, one nested inside the other.
explanation.definitionFit: A dandy who fusses over clothes and style is said to be foppish.

clue.text: Sources of timber for endless trestles

indicators.note: the little word 'for' loses its last letter, having no end

parts.note: trestles are supports or rests

explanation.surface: Wood supply for trestle tables that never run out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' acts only on 'for', giving FO; it does not cut 'trestles'.
explanation.definitionFit: Large wooded areas supply wood for building.

clue.text: One used to carrying a load?

definitions.text: One used to carrying a load?

parts.words: One used to carrying a load?
parts.note: the load is a load of money, so this is a very rich person rather than a porter

explanation.surface: A porter accustomed to heavy burdens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a load' is slang for lots of money.
explanation.definitionFit: A person whose power comes from great wealth carries a fortune.

clue.text: Addition to dress produced by pins, etc

indicators.note: the answer is produced by the run of letters across the words that follow

explanation.surface: A dressmaker's extra piece made with pins and so on.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit across 'pINS ETc'.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece of material set into a garment is an inset.

clue.text: Lady's fate, interwoven with HM's future

parts.note: her is the possessive for a lady

indicators.note: the fate letters and the monarch letters are woven together and rearranged

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, was Her Majesty

explanation.surface: A lady's destiny entwined with the monarch's future.
explanation.walkthrough: 'interwoven with' mixes the four letters of 'fate' with the monarch's two letters to give EAFTER, which follows the lady's pronoun.
explanation.definitionFit: The life to come, or time ahead, is the hereafter.

clue.text: Meal's recipe is German

parts.note: R is the standard abbreviation for recipe, from Latin 'recipe' (take)
Otto is a typical German man's name

explanation.surface: A dish's cooking instructions are German in origin.
explanation.walkthrough: R for recipe is the old prescription abbreviation; any German name standing for 'German' is a crossword habit.
explanation.definitionFit: An Italian rice dish cooked in stock makes a complete meal.

clue.text: Cook fish that's strong

parts.note: to rig is to fiddle, as in cooking the books
the id or ide is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: Prepare a fish that has a powerful flavour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cook' is not kitchen work but fixing dishonestly.
explanation.definitionFit: Something stiff and unbending is firm and sturdy.

clue.text: Birds with shiny features pecking plant

indicators.note: the plant gets inside the shiny features, as a beak pecks into something

parts.note: stars shine in the night sky
ling is heather

explanation.surface: Birds with glossy plumage peck at a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pecking' is a container signal: the heather word is driven into the shiny features as a beak drives in.
explanation.definitionFit: Glossy speckled songbirds that gather in large flocks are starlings.

clue.text: Hawk's snaffled river fish

indicators.note: to snaffle is to grab, so the hawk word grabs the river letter inside it

parts.note: to hawk is to tout, to sell aggressively

explanation.surface: A bird of prey has grabbed a fish from the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hawk' looks like the bird but is the verb to peddle.
explanation.definitionFit: A freshwater game fish related to salmon.

clue.text: Foreign article appended to old literature

indicators.note: the article is added at the end of the other pieces

parts.note: verse is poetic literature
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An overseas article tacked on to some ancient writing.
explanation.definitionFit: Overseas or abroad means from a foreign land.

clue.text: Beats paths out of East

indicators.note: the compass letter is taken out of the word for paths, so 'out of' signals the removal

parts.note: routes are paths or courses

explanation.surface: Someone strikes out paths heading out of the East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' removes E from ROUTES. 'Beats' is a verb here: to defeat heavily.
explanation.definitionFit: Inflicting a crushing defeat on an army or team is to rout it, as 'beats' says.

clue.text: Set up academic function and procedure

parts.note: to rig is to set up or fit out
MA, Master of Arts, is a holder of an academic degree
a role is a function or job

explanation.surface: Organising a university ceremony and its formalities.
explanation.definitionFit: A long, fussy procedure is called a rigmarole.

clue.text: The symbols required by a dictator?

definitions.text: The symbols required by a dictator?

parts.words: The symbols required by a dictator?
parts.note: a dictator here is someone dictating letters to a secretary, who records them in quick written symbols, not a tyrant

explanation.surface: A tyrant needs emblems and insignia to rule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dictator' suggests a despot; the sense is someone who dictates to a typist.
explanation.definitionFit: Pitman's and Gregg's are systems of quick symbols used to take down dictation.

clue.text: Plant from mountains round Uruguay

indicators.note: the word for mountains goes round the country letter, which 'round' signals

parts.note: mountains of something means lots of it
U is the international vehicle code for Uruguay

explanation.surface: A flower brought back from high peaks near Uruguay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mountains' tempts as ALPS or similar, but it means 'lots', as in mountains of work.
explanation.definitionFit: The water lily of Asia, sacred in Buddhism, is a well-known aquatic plant.

clue.text: Sprinkle plants needing to I be coaxed back

indicators.note: the plants are drawn back the other way, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: worts are plants, as in St John's wort

explanation.surface: Scatter seed for plants that must be coaxed into returning.
explanation.walkthrough: The page has a stray 'I' from scanning. 'coaxed back' turns WORTS round. STROW is an old form of strew.
explanation.definitionFit: To strew or scatter, as with rushes on a floor, is the archaic verb strow.

clue.text: Extensive drink pickles (they say) up top

indicators.note: in a down clue, the pickles piece goes above the drink
the word for pickles is spoken, giving a different spelling

parts.note: pickles are holes, tight spots
ale is beer

explanation.surface: A huge drink of pickles goes to the head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pickles' are scrapes; HOLES sounds like WHOLES.
explanation.definitionFit: Done on a big scale without discrimination, as in wholesale changes.

clue.text: Spider worker's joining Union, note, after rejection of scab

indicators.note: the worker, union and note follow the turned scab word
rejecting the word for scab turns it back, so its letters are read backwards

parts.note: a rat is a strikebreaker, a scab
an ant is the classic crossword worker
la is the sixth note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A labourer joins the union and writes a note after spurning a strikebreaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejection of' turns the scab word round to give TAR; 'after' puts the rest behind it. The labour-dispute surface hides two creatures.
explanation.definitionFit: A large hairy spider of southern Europe and the Americas is a tarantula.

clue.text: Ticket holder pockets small amount, fifth among prizes

indicators.note: the holder takes the other pieces inside it as a pocket would

parts.note: a rack holds things
an inch is a small amount

indicators.note: the fifth letter of prizes is taken

explanation.surface: A ticket-holder pockets a little cash, the fifth among the prizes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pockets' is a container signal; 'fifth among prizes' gives E, the fifth letter of that word. A rain check is a ticket for a later date when an event is rained off.
explanation.definitionFit: A voucher for a later show when an event is rained off is a ticket.

clue.text: Uniform and shirt removed from laundrette, crumpled

indicators.note: crumpled clothes are rearranged, so the letters are mixed
the shirt letter is taken out of the laundrette word

parts.note: T stands for a T-shirt

explanation.surface: A uniform and shirt taken from a launderette come out creased.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uniform' looks like clothing in the laundry scene, but it is the definition: an adjective meaning unchanging.
explanation.definitionFit: Something consistent throughout has not been changed.

clue.text: Tuning up prior to medley

indicators.note: tuning adjusts and resets the letters of the words that follow, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: An orchestra tunes up before playing a selection of pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tuning' reworks UP PRIOR TO, all nine letters. 'medley' looks musical but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A mixture of dried petals, or any miscellany, is a potpourri.

clue.text: Hunt for work

explanation.definitionFit: A chase is one sense; an occupation or hobby followed is the other.

clue.text: Inundate Exchange, investing millions

indicators.note: to invest is to clothe or surround, so the exchange word wraps the M

parts.note: to swap is to exchange
M stands for million(s)

explanation.surface: Flood the Stock Exchange by putting millions into it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'investing' is a container signal, not finance: M goes inside SWAP.
explanation.definitionFit: To overwhelm with water or work is to swamp.

clue.text: Stage pro wearing artificial hairstyle

indicators.note: the hairstyle surrounds the pro word as if wearing it

parts.note: a perm is a chemically set hairstyle
pro means for

explanation.surface: A professional sports a fake hairdo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pro' means in favour of, FOR, not professional.
explanation.definitionFit: To stage a play is to put it on, to present it.

clue.text: Audibly criticise 'entertainment

indicators.note: the critic's word is spoken, and its sound gives the answer

parts.note: to review is to criticise or assess a work

explanation.surface: Loudly slate a show.
explanation.definitionFit: A stage show of sketches, songs and dances is a theatrical entertainment.

clue.text: Floor reportedly has old look

indicators.note: the floor word is heard, and its sound is spelt differently

parts.note: a deck is a floor of a ship

explanation.surface: The floor is said to look old.
explanation.walkthrough: DEKKO is British slang for a quick look, from Hindi.
explanation.definitionFit: A quick look or glance is a dekko in British slang.

clue.text: Black storm over North

indicators.note: in a down clue the storm word sits over the north letter

parts.note: to rave is to storm or rant

explanation.surface: A black storm is coming over from the north.
explanation.definitionFit: Glossy black is called raven, like the bird's feathers.

clue.text: A French shanty on the French release

parts.note: un is French for 'a'
a shanty is a shack, a crude hut
le is French for 'the'

explanation.surface: A French shack on the French coast is set free.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shanty' suggests a sea song; here it is a hut.
explanation.definitionFit: To unchain or free someone is to release them from restraint.

clue.text: Six and King fit, making a "house'

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals
R is short for rex, king
go means fit, as in 'it won't go in the box'

explanation.surface: Six people and a monarch make a household.
explanation.walkthrough: In astrology the zodiac signs are called houses.
explanation.definitionFit: The sign of the Virgin is one of the twelve zodiac divisions astrologers call houses.

clue.text: Ray's the one likely to get fired

definitions.meaning: the electric ray is a flat fish that stuns its prey

definitions.text: the one likely to get fired
definitions.meaning: a missile launched from a submarine

explanation.surface: Ray is the employee who will be sacked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ray' looks like a man's name; 'fired' looks like sacked.
explanation.definitionFit: The electric ray fish shares its name with the underwater missile launched from a tube.

clue.text: Family title reinforced by grand political status

indicators.note: the grand letter is put into the middle of the family and title words, strengthening them from within

parts.note: kin are family
Dom is a title given to some monks
G stands for grand, a thousand pounds

explanation.surface: A family's title is strengthened by grand political standing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reinforced by' is a container signal: the grand letter is set between the family and title words to strengthen them.
explanation.definitionFit: A realm ruled by a monarch is a state, a political standing among nations.
